themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 5 reports this week compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—signaling either a coordinated posting campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates this is a severe statistical anomaly
Single-week spike suggests acute event rather than chronic condition
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods or blocks being targeted? Map complaint clusters.
Is this related to political campaigns, business advertising, or gang activity?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Contractor Failure
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped to 14 reports last week versus a 2.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 433% spike (z-score: 5.1)—indicating a potential breakdown in garbage pickup service across Central Harlem.
evidence: 14 missed collection complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase)
Timing aligns with broader unsanitary condition complaints (1,280 total over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Which sanitation routes are affected? Are specific blocks being systematically missed?
Is this a staffing shortage, equipment failure, or contractor scheduling issue?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints reached 7 reports last week compared to a 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—an 833% spike (z-score: 4.81)—marking a significant increase in vandalism across Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (833% increase)
Z-score of 4.81 indicates highly significant spike
Clusters with illegal posting spike, suggesting broader public space disturbance
reporting_angles: Are specific corridors or institutions being targeted (transit, schools, storefronts)?
Is this gang-related tagging or opportunistic vandalism during enforcement gaps?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 8 reports last week versus a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,500% spike (z-score: 5.67)—suggesting either aggressive city enforcement action or an influx of illegal street vending in Central Harlem.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,500% increase)
Z-score of 5.67 confirms extreme statistical anomaly
Converges with illegal posting spike, suggesting simultaneous public space violations
reporting_angles: Has the city launched a targeted enforcement campaign this week? Contact NYPD Street Enforcement Task Force.
Are vendors responding to new market demand or has illegal vending expanded due to enforcement gaps elsewhere?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints spiked to 13 reports two weeks ago versus a 3.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 236% increase (z-score: 3.42)—indicating a growing problem with derelict cars cluttering Central Harlem neighborhoods.
evidence: 13 abandoned vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (236% increase)
Converges with illegal parking spike (146 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 82.2 average, up 78%)
reporting_angles: What specific blocks have the highest concentration of abandoned vehicles? Are they creating safety or environmental hazards?
Is NYPD responding to tow requests? What is the average wait time for removal?
